outcomes.name: Classical ML engineer, tabular problems
outcomes.rationale: Overlaps sklearn/PyTorch on many skills, but every signal here is tabular: SQL, regression, gradient boosting, cross-validation, and no model-serving or infrastructure skills. Feature engineering and model selection at 4 are the core of the role at weight 0.75/0.70. This is the archetype the role was written for.

outcomes.name: ML engineer moving toward deep learning
outcomes.rationale: PyTorch and neural networks at 4 make the deep-learning half real, but this profile has no MLOps, no cloud, and thin SQL. The ML Engineer role weights scikit-learn and PyTorch highest and asks only 0.6 of Docker, so it fits better than a Deep Learning Engineer role that would demand far more neural-network depth.

outcomes.name: ML engineer with a serving focus
outcomes.rationale: Classical plus serving. Docker and FastAPI at 4 are the tie-breaker: the AI Engineer role would score this higher, but the ML Engineer role weights Docker 0.68 and does not require cloud, and this profile has no AWS at all. Deliberately near the AI Engineer / ML Engineer boundary.
outcomes.note: boundary: AI Engineer is a plausible alternative

outcomes.name: Full-stack AI product engineer
outcomes.rationale: Balanced across modelling, serving, and infrastructure, which is exactly the AI Engineer role's shape. It is deliberately weaker than the ML Engineer archetype on model selection and cross-validation (absent) and stronger on CI/CD, monitoring and AWS, which the AI Engineer role weights and the ML Engineer role does not.

outcomes.name: AI engineer, backend-leaning
outcomes.rationale: Strong on the service and data side, thin on modelling (scikit-learn 3, PyTorch 2). That combination is the AI Engineer role's signature: it needs Python, SQL, Docker, FastAPI and AWS far more than it needs deep-learning depth. Weak enough to be a plausible MLOps Engineer, but MLOps wants Kubernetes and Terraform, which are absent.
outcomes.note: boundary: MLOps Engineer is a plausible alternative

outcomes.name: Experimentation-focused product data scientist
outcomes.rationale: The Data Scientist role in its purest form: statistics, hypothesis testing, and A/B testing all at 5, with SQL at 5. Little infrastructure, no deployment. The weight on experimentation and hypothesis testing is what separates this from a Data Engineer, who would have pipelines and warehousing instead.

outcomes.name: Time-series forecasting data scientist
outcomes.rationale: Forecasting is the single strongest signal here and it is the role's name. Ranks across every family in this profile. The time-series skill set is dense and the forecasting role is the only one that requires it at high weight, so the discrimination should be clean even though the profile is small.

outcomes.name: Data scientist moving toward ML
outcomes.rationale: Linear algebra and calculus at 4, transformers and attention at 3, and no dashboards, no A/B testing, no business communication. That is a research-shaped profile. It is deliberately near the boundary with Machine Learning Engineer, which would fit it too.
outcomes.note: boundary: Machine Learning Engineer is a plausible alternative

outcomes.name: Business-facing analyst
outcomes.rationale: SQL and Excel at 5, no model training at all, regression only at 2. The Data Analyst role is the only one in the knowledge base whose highest-weight skills are SQL, Python and Pandas with a very low modelling requirement, so this should discriminate cleanly against Data Scientist.

outcomes.name: Streaming data engineer
outcomes.rationale: Spark, Kafka, Airflow and streaming all present at 4. The Data Engineer role is the only one that requires a streaming weight of 0.8, so a profile with genuine streaming experience should separate from a batch-only data engineer cleanly.

outcomes.name: Analytics engineer, modelling focused
outcomes.rationale: dbt and dimensional modelling at 5 with SQL at 5 and no Spark. That is the Analytics Engineer signature. The Data Engineer role would want distributed processing skills this profile entirely lacks.

outcomes.name: Senior data engineer with governance ownership
outcomes.rationale: Airflow, data modelling and governance all at 5, which is the Senior Data Engineer profile: the extra weight the senior role places on governance, documentation and mentoring is exactly what is present here.

outcomes.name: MLOps engineer, platform focused
outcomes.rationale: Docker, Linux and Bash at 5 with Kubernetes and CI/CD at 4. The MLOps Engineer role is the only one weighting Docker above 0.9, so the Docker proficiency is what should carry this profile.

outcomes.name: ML infrastructure engineer
outcomes.rationale: Kubernetes at 5, AWS at 5, Terraform and distributed systems at 4, and deep modelling knowledge only at 2. That is the infrastructure-leadership profile: the Infrastructure Engineer role weights scalability and cost above modelling, which is the inverse of the MLOps Engineer role.

outcomes.name: DevOps engineer with no ML focus
outcomes.rationale: Strong CI/CD, Jenkins and shell, with no machine-learning skill at all. That is the DevOps Engineer role, not the MLOps Engineer role: MLOps requires mlflow, mlops and model-monitoring which are entirely absent, and this profile has more Jenkins and shell than any MLOps profile.

outcomes.name: Classical NLP pipeline engineer
outcomes.rationale: spaCy at 5 and NLTK at 4 with tokenisation, NER and text classification at 4. The NLP Engineer role is the only one requiring spaCy near 1.0, so that is the discriminating skill here.

outcomes.name: LLM application engineer, retrieval focused
outcomes.rationale: Prompt engineering and RAG both at 5, with vector databases and LangChain. The Generative AI Engineer and LLM Engineer roles both fit; the LLM Engineer role weights evaluation and serving higher, which is the tie-breaker.
outcomes.note: boundary: Generative AI Engineer is a plausible alternative

outcomes.name: Speech and audio engineer
outcomes.rationale: speech-recognition at 5 with audio processing, signal processing and CTC. Only one role in the knowledge base requires speech recognition, so this should be the cleanest discrimination in the whole set.

outcomes.name: LLM engineer, model-side focus
outcomes.rationale: Transformers and tokenisation at 5, Hugging Face at 5, PyTorch at 4, and almost no application-layer work (prompt engineering 3, RAG 3). The LLM Engineer role is the one that weights tokenisation and Transformers near 1.0, so it should beat the Generative AI Engineer role here.

outcomes.name: Computer vision engineer
outcomes.rationale: cnn, computer-vision and PyTorch all at 5, with detection and segmentation at 4 and OpenCV augmentation present. The strongest single-domain profile in the set; the risk here is false confidence, not difficulty.

outcomes.name: Research scientist, optimisation focus
outcomes.rationale: Linear algebra at 5 and the mathematics core at 4, with experimental design and hypothesis testing present and no product or infrastructure work at all. That is the research profile the scientist role was written for.

outcomes.name: Research engineer, NLP focus
outcomes.rationale: Transformers, self-supervised learning and transfer learning at 4 with a full mathematics core and no product work. The Research Engineer role is the one that combines a methods core with ablations, which is exactly the shape here.

outcomes.name: Fraud analyst
outcomes.rationale: Anomaly detection and feature engineering both at 5, with SHAP for investigator explanation and explicit handling of imbalanced data. The Fraud Analyst role is the only one requiring anomaly detection at 0.9.

outcomes.name: Quantitative researcher, time series
outcomes.rationale: Backtesting and time-series analysis both at 5 with a full quantitative core. Look-ahead-bias-free evaluation is the distinguishing competence, and the Quantitative Researcher role is the only one weighting backtesting near 1.0.

outcomes.name: Sparse undergraduate, no production experience
outcomes.rationale: Deliberately sparse: four skills at 1-3. Included because a profile set where every candidate matches at 90% tests nothing. Every coverage component will be small, and the top-1 rank is genuinely uncertain - which is the honest answer for a user with almost nothing to declare.
outcomes.note: thin profile: coverage is low everywhere; top-1 is expected to be unstable

outcomes.name: Backend engineer with no AI/ML exposure
outcomes.rationale: Strong general backend with no machine-learning skill whatsoever. Included to check the engine does not drift toward an unrelated role when the AI/ML signal is absent. The Backend Engineer role is the only one that asks for SQL and PostgreSQL at 1.0 and 0.95 with no ML requirement at all.
